reviewed_proof_scopes.semantic_scope: Machine-learning score formulas, finite choice functions, labels, q-acceptance, strict total orders, and top-q queues.
Choice distance, instability, variability, ML representation, substitutability, and all three clauses of Theorem 1.
Sequential composition and the upper, lower, and single-order clauses of Theorem 2.
The four concrete NYC program classes and Proposition 2 exact variability claims.
Choice-property lemmas, distance algebra, zero instability, independence, one-instability, parity, and tight-instability constructions.
General variability, append/remove equivalence, ranking-m, q-representative equivalence, sequential substitutability, and additive variability.
Linear-assignment model and proofs, ML representation proof, and the concrete program-witness proof sketch.

defects.source_claim: The printed no-zero-instability clause omits q>0 and a nontrivial universe with more than q applicants.
defects.status_impact_rationale: These are minor implicit nondegeneracy conditions; Lean proves the advertised capacity phenomenon on its mathematically meaningful domain.
defects.repair_obligation: State and prove the no-zero endpoint with positive capacity and an input pool strictly larger than capacity.
defects.acceptance_condition: A paper-facing theorem derives non-zero instability from feasibility, q-acceptance, q>0, and q<|U|.
defects.resolution_evidence: paper_no_zero_instability_under_capacity_statement exposes exactly the corrected domain and conclusion.

defects.source_claim: The proof assumes two disjoint q-element sets although |U|>q alone does not imply |U|≥2q.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The theorem endpoint is correct and Lean proves it by a one-extra-applicant argument, so the flaw is confined to the printed proof route.
defects.repair_obligation: Prove monotonicity/q-acceptance incompatibility from one q-set plus one additional applicant, without a 2q-cardinality premise.
defects.acceptance_condition: The contradiction follows under exactly q≥1 and q<|U|.
defects.resolution_evidence: paper_monotonicity_q_acceptance_incompatible_statement proves the endpoint under the original theorem conditions.

defects.source_claim: The lemma conclusion prints V_C(X₁)=V_C(X₁), while the proof and use require V_C(X₁)=V_C(X₂).
defects.status_impact_rationale: This is an obvious self-equality typo; Lean proves the intended cross-pool equality and no substantive claim changes.
defects.repair_obligation: Replace the second X₁ by X₂ and prove the intended equality from equal chosen sets.
defects.acceptance_condition: The corrected cross-pool equality is a theorem after deriving substitutability from q-acceptance and 1-instability.

defects.source_claim: The corollary says tightly dk-unstable although d is the even instability parameter and k is not part of the statement.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The typo does not alter the corollary's intended no-positive-even-tightness endpoint, which Lean proves parametrically.
defects.repair_obligation: Read the corollary as excluding tightly d-unstable rules for positive even d.
defects.acceptance_condition: Lean proves every positive even 2k bound improves to 2k-1 under consistency.

defects.source_claim: The union expression contains the stray token /X'_i instead of X'_i.
defects.status_impact_rationale: This is a typesetting token in an intermediate construction; the maximum-equality endpoint is represented by checked equivalence theorems.
defects.repair_obligation: Use X=⋃_i X'_i=X₀∪{x'_1,…,x'_m} in the second direction.
defects.acceptance_condition: Both at-most and exact insertion/removal variability predicates are proved equivalent.
defects.resolution_evidence: The two append/remove equivalence rows expose the corrected endpoint.

defects.source_claim: The proof prints X'\{x'})=X with an unmatched closing parenthesis.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The unmatched parenthesis is typographical and does not itself change the intended set identity.
defects.acceptance_condition: The formal statement uses insert/remove pools with the intended identity.
defects.resolution_evidence: The ranking-m paper-facing rows use X and insert x X consistently.

defects.source_claim: The LAP instability proof ends with |C(X')|>|C(X')|, an impossible self-comparison; the intended comparison is |C(X')|>|C(X)|=q.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The self-comparison is a local proof typo; the real-weight canonical LAP instability theorem proves the intended endpoint.
defects.repair_obligation: Use q-acceptance to compare C(X') with C(X), not with itself.
defects.acceptance_condition: The selector-level instability proof derives the capacity contradiction without a self-comparison.

defects.source_claim: The proof writes x'≠C(X') where the required assertion is x'∉C(X').
defects.status_impact_rationale: This is a set-membership typo in the parity argument and does not change the theorem's intended endpoint.
defects.repair_obligation: Replace object/set inequality by nonmembership and connect it to the indicator parity.
defects.acceptance_condition: Lean derives fresh-applicant nonselection from positive even distance and concludes inconsistency.

defects.source_claim: The proof says one of x_{s_j} or x_{s_j} is excluded; the first occurrence should be x_{s_i}.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The repeated index is a minor local typo; it does not change the distinct-slot-order variability claim.
defects.repair_obligation: Compare x_{s_i} and x_{s_j} under their shared order and exclude the nonminimal one.
defects.acceptance_condition: The formal class-count argument distinguishes the two assigned applicants.
defects.resolution_evidence: paper_lap_assigned_strictly_outranks_rejected_statement and the canonical distinct-order variability theorem

defects.source_claim: Completeness is printed for all x₁,x₂, which conflicts with asymmetry when x₁=x₂; the standard strict-order condition compares distinct pairs.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The standard distinct-pair repair is minor and is exactly the semantics used throughout the paper and Lean.
defects.acceptance_condition: The q-representative model is built over an asymmetric, transitive, distinct-pair total relation.
defects.resolution_evidence: paper_definition_total_order uses the coherent strict-total-order predicate.

defects.acceptance_condition: Lean constructs the score/threshold rule and derives independence and zero instability without assuming independence.
